thread:
mike: putting this RFC follow-up here — we sketched shard ownership for the new rate-limiter but didn't fully land on the tradeoffs. quick brain dump and questions below.

lina: perfect, thanks. main thing i'm worried about is cross-shard coordination overhead for soft-fallbacks when a shard is overloaded. can we avoid synchronous cross-shard calls? :thinking_face:

raj: i don't want a global coordinator either. my rough idea: deterministic tenant->shard mapping + per-shard local fairness, then an async rebalancer that nudges heavy tenants across shards during low load windows.

anya: agree with raj. two followups: how do we handle tenant bursts that exceed single-shard capacity before rebalancer moves them? and how do we keep abuse signals consistent across shards?

mike: for bursts we discussed local provisional admits with short-lived tokens and circuit breakers. simple heuristics: if a tenant uses >X tokens/s for Y seconds, mark provisional and rate-limit locally while rebalancer plans migration.

lina: provisional admits are fine but the problem is fairness: if shard A is full and shards B/C are idle, the tenant on A shouldn't starve other tenants on A. we need a local soft cap and a cheap signal to indicate other shards can accept spill.

raj: cheap signal = bloom-filtered shard-availability beacon? like each shard periodically publishes a small advert with available credit buckets. makes migration decision local and asynchronous.

anya: bloom filters might be noisy; false positives are okay but false negatives hurt. also we need a consistent abuse score for tenant across shards. proposal: central abuse service with eventual consistency (writes are idempotent, shards read last-known score).

jamie: central abuse service is okay if read path is local cache + ttl. don't call it synchronously on every request. update cadence 1s-5s should be fine for most cases.

mike: ops concern: if we rely on rebalancer + adverts, what about failure modes? shard crash during migration, or ads stale -> tenant duplicates on multiple shards. need anti-duplication guard.

lina: anti-duplication: each tenant admission slot has a namespace+lease id. only one shard can hold an active lease for a tenant's primary credit window. if duplicate detected, lease leasing service resolves by comparing last-updated timestamp and rotating.

raj: that's basically a lightweight lease service — could be implemented on top of existing token bank metadata with optimistic concurrency. avoids full-blown consensus for every request.

anya: tradeoff: adds extra writes on migration paths. but reads remain local. also helps observability — you can trace which shard currently owns a tenant.

jamie: what about quotas across models (multi-dimensional quotas)? shard mapping should be by tenant, but internal per-model accounting needs to be composable. we shouldn't shard-models separately else coordination explodes.

mike: agree: shard by tenant id. per-shard accounting tracks per-model counters. global quota evaluation (e.g., tenant-level cap across models) can be approximate via cached aggregates; hard limits require a quick check with central quota service in slow path.

lina: slow path calls should be rare. define SLO: 99.9% of requests only touch local shard, slow path <0.1%. we'll validate with canary.

raj: rollout plan: 1) deterministic hash mapping + local fairness for low risk tenants. 2) enable adverts + provisional admits for canary 10% of traffic. 3) tenant lease/lease-service for migration. 4) rebalancer enabled in read-only to produce suggestions, then active migration.

anya: monitoring checklist: tenant-level latencies, provisional admit rates, adverts staleness, lease collisions, abuse-score divergence. create dashboards before enabling rebalancer.

mike: ops playbook: if rebalancer causes oscillation, we fallback to reservoir-mode: limit migrations and increase provisional admit thresholds. add rate-limiter feature flag to quickly pin tenants to shards.

jamie: experiment idea: simulate 10k tenants with real burst profiles and run rebalancer to measure oscillation amplitude. we should run both synthetic and traffic-replay tests.

lina: +1. i'll sketch the simulation and share. also: small config API needed for per-tenant migration windows and provisional thresholds.

raj: pbkdf: don't forget security: shard adverts and lease APIs must be authenticated and namespaced per-region to avoid cross-tenant data leaks.

mike: good call. ops-bot: can you create an RFC follow-up ticket with the rollout steps, monitoring checklist, and simulation tasks? :robot_face:

ops-bot: created ticket INFRA-1629 "rate-limiter shard ownership & rebalancer rollout" and linked this thread.

anya: thanks. i'll take the abuse-score consistency design and write a proposal for the lease semantics.

lina: i'll own simulation + dashboards.

raj: i'll prototype the advert format and lightweight lease implementation.

mike: thanks everyone. next sync on this in infra weekly; we'll move tickets and aim to canary in two sprints. :rocket:
